minutes.headline: Committee adopted amended operating protocols and agreed to redraft a primary-school mini-split warrant article for its next meeting.
minutes.summary: After an executive session on non-union negotiations, the committee reviewed its operating protocols section by section, adding language on superintendent direction, community trust, tabling items when meetings run long, and MASC orientation timing. It reviewed last year's goals and floated ideas for new ones, to be set at a later meeting. It also discussed Turkey Hill ADA/MSBA funding and the primary school air conditioning warrant article, voting to rewrite the article.

decisions.decision: Add a protocol line that the superintendent takes direction from the committee as a whole, not from a single member.
Add the community and staff to the protocol on building trust.
Add protocol language that agenda items not time-sensitive may be tabled if a meeting runs long.
Change the MASC orientation requirement to within one year of being seated.
Set goals at the second September meeting; members to send ideas ahead.
The warrant article wording will be reworked and taken up at the next meeting on the 6th.

what_happened.line: The School Committee voted to accept its operating protocols as amended after going through them section by section.
The committee voted to rewrite the warrant article for a primary school mini-split project and bring improved language to the next meeting on the 6th.
Members said the capital plan appropriation covered only a fraction of full air conditioning, so town meeting would be asked to reappropriate it to mini-splits.
The committee added protocol language letting non-urgent agenda items be tabled when meetings run long, and set MASC orientation within one year of being seated.

Turkey Hill ADA funding stayed unresolved: a pending ARPA request and a special town meeting article were named as options, and the superintendent had been told MSBA would not fund an ADA-only project.

why_it_matters: The primary school cooling plan is headed to town meeting as a request to repurpose existing capital money, so residents may be asked to vote on the reappropriation and on how far it goes toward air conditioning.
Turkey Hill accessibility work and athletic turf replacement both have funding questions still open, and either could reach a warrant or the budget as a new request.
